title: Kunneth formula, one proper factor, integer coefficients
statement:
Let $k$ be a separably closed
field. Let $X$ be a
proper scheme over $k$
and let $Y$ be a
quasi-compact and
quasi-separated scheme over $k$. If $E\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ has
torsion cohomology and
$K\in\Dplus(Y_{\Et})$, then the Kunneth map of
[def-kun-kunneth-map] for the square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X\times_kY&\xrightarrow{\;\operatorname{pr}_2\;}&Y\\
\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle \operatorname{pr}_1}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle a_Y}\\
X&\xrightarrow{\;a_X\;}&\Spec(k)
\end{array}
$$

$$
\kappa_{E,K}:
\RGamma(X_{\Et},E)\kunotimes{\mathbf Z}\RGamma(Y_{\Et},K)
\longrightarrow
\RGamma\bigl((X\times_kY)_{\Et},
\pr_1^{-1}E\kunotimes{\mathbf Z}\pr_2^{-1}K\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism. (*Source:* Stacks Project, Tag
[0F14](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F14), part (1).)

proof.text: Put $S=\Spec(k)$, $W=X\times_kY$, $p=\operatorname{pr}_1$, $q=\operatorname{pr}_2$, $f=a_X$, $g=a_Y$, and $c=f p=g q$. Set $E'=p^{-1}E$ and $K'=q^{-1}K$. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] inverse image is exact. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to a representing complex gives $\mathcal H^i(E')=p^{-1}\mathcal H^i(E)$ and $\mathcal H^i(K')=q^{-1}\mathcal H^i(K)$. These vanish below the respective lower bounds of $E,K$; hence both inverse images are bounded below. Each $p^{-1}\mathcal H^i(E)$ is torsion by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-torsion], so $E'$ has torsion cohomology. Finally [lem-kun-proper-stability] makes $q$ proper, since it is the base change of the proper $f$. These verify all the hypotheses for the integer-coefficient proper projection formula below.

source.place: Tag 0F14, label lemma-kunneth-one-proper, proof (1), first sentence; exact inverse image: Tag 03Q1, label lemma-stalk-pullback (1), and homology.tex Tag 010N, label lemma-exact-functor

proof.text: We make explicit the point-topos identification used in proper base change. By [lem-kun-0ezp] every etale $U\to S$ is a disjoint union $\coprod_{i\in I}S$. Sheaf gluing over the component cover gives $F(U)=\prod_{i\in I}F(S)$ for every abelian sheaf $F$, naturally under maps of such objects. The constant sheaf with value an abelian group $M$ in [def-kun-constant-sheaf] has the same formula $\underline M(U)=\prod_{i\in I}M$. Thus the evaluation maps $\underline{F(S)}\to F$ and $M\to\underline M(S)$ are inverse natural identifications: sections on $S$ and the constant-sheaf functor are inverse exact equivalences. These equivalences also identify tensor products: after restriction to each component $S$, the universal property of the sheaf tensor is the universal property of the tensor of the two section groups. Applied termwise, the equivalences preserve cohomology and quasi-isomorphisms and identify $D(S_{\Et})$ with $D(\mathbf Z)$, including bounded-below objects. They preserve K-flat complexes, since the tensor with each acyclic complex corresponds to the tensor with its acyclic image under the inverse equivalence; consequently this identification respects derived tensor and its sign symmetry. In particular, for any complex $J$ on $S$, $J\cong\underline{\RGamma(S_{\Et},J)}$: exactness of evaluation makes its derived functor equal to evaluation itself, using the resolution recipe of [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded].

source.place: Tag 0F14, label lemma-kunneth-one-proper, proof (1), identification after proper base change; point-site decomposition as in lem-kun-0ezp, using the component covering and the sheaf axiom

proof.text: Let $A=\RGamma(X_{\Et},E)$ and $B=Rq_*E'$. If $E$ has no cohomology below $b$, then $Rf_*E$ has none below $b$ by [lem-kun-tensor-t-est]. By [lem-kun-leray-bdd] for $f$, $A\cong\RGamma(S_{\Et},Rf_*E)$; step 2 identifies $Rf_*E$ with $\underline A$, and shows $A\in D^+(\mathbf Z)$. The square $(p,q,f,g)$ is cartesian and $f$ is proper; $E$ is bounded below with torsion cohomology, so [thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below] gives the canonical exchange isomorphism $g^{-1}Rf_*E\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_*p^{-1}E=B$. The constant-object identification and [lem-kun-pullback-constant] identify its source with $\underline A$ on $Y_{\Et}$. Consequently $B\cong\underline A$, by the inverse of this exchange isomorphism. No finite-type hypothesis on $Y$, nor invertibility hypothesis on the orders of the torsion, has been used.

source.place: Tag 0F14, label lemma-kunneth-one-proper, proof (1), second displayed identification; proper base change Tag 0DDE, label lemma-proper-base-change

proof.text: Put $T=E'\kunotimes{\mathbf Z}K'\in D(W_{\Et})$. Apply [lem-kun-0f0f] to the proper $q:W\to Y$, the bounded-below torsion-cohomology object $E'$ of step 1, and $K\in D^+(Y_{\Et})$. It states that the canonical map $B\kunotimes{\mathbf Z}K\longrightarrow Rq_*T$ is an isomorphism. We shall use its inverse, $Rq_*T\xrightarrow{\sim}B\kunotimes{\mathbf Z}K$, followed by the isomorphism $B\cong\underline A$ of step 3.

source.place: Tag 0F14, label lemma-kunneth-one-proper, proof (1), first display; Tag 0F0F, label lemma-projection-formula-proper

proof.text: For clarity the Leray comparison can be taken on the whole derived category, so it needs no additional assertion about the lower bound of $T$. Use the small presentations fixed in [def-weil-size-convention], and apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to the etale topoi with constant ring $\mathbf Z$, and to $q:W\to Y$, $g:Y\to S$. It gives $Rc_*T\cong Rg_*Rq_*T$. Evaluating on $S$ is exact by step 2. The recipe of [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded] identifies evaluation of $Ra_{Z,*}H$ with $\RGamma(Z_{\Et},H)$: on a K-injective resolution $I$ of $H$ it is the identity $\Gamma(S,a_{Z,*}I)=\Gamma(Z,I)$. More explicitly, choose a K-injective representative $I$ of $T$ and a K-injective resolution $j:q_*I\to J$. The cited composition theorem says $g_*j$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Exact evaluation on $S$ makes $\Gamma(S,g_*j)=\Gamma(Y,j)$ a quasi-isomorphism from $\Gamma(W,I)$ to $\Gamma(Y,J)$. These are the defining representatives of $\RGamma(W_{\Et},T)$ and $\RGamma(Y_{\Et},Rq_*T)$, so their comparison is an isomorphism. This is the canonical derived-functor composition comparison, whose bounded-below restriction is the Leray comparison in the blueprint; no finite-cohomological-dimension theorem is required.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, label lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; this supplies the Leray composition used in etale-cohomology.tex Tag 0F14, label lemma-kunneth-one-proper, proof (1)

proof.text: Composing steps 3--5 identifies $\RGamma(W_{\Et},T)$ with $\RGamma(Y_{\Et},\underline A\kunotimes{\mathbf Z}K)$. Use [lem-kun-tensor-sym] on $Y_{\Et}$ to rewrite the latter as $\RGamma(Y_{\Et},K\kunotimes{\mathbf Z}\underline A)$. Since $Y$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, $K\in D^+(Y_{\Et})$, and $A\in D^+(\mathbf Z)$ by step 3, [lem-kun-0f0e] with its variables $E:=K$ and constant complex $K:=A$ supplies the inverse isomorphism to $\RGamma(Y_{\Et},K)\kunotimes{\mathbf Z}A$. A final symmetry gives $A\kunotimes{\mathbf Z}\RGamma(Y_{\Et},K)$. Here symmetry in $D(\mathbf Z)$ is the instance of [lem-kun-tensor-sym] on $S_{\Et}$ under the constant-sheaf/evaluation equivalence of step 2: the termwise tensor and its sign symmetry become the ordinary ones. Denote the resulting composite isomorphism by $\theta$. This is precisely the Leray, inverse proper projection formula, inverse proper exchange, constant-complex projection formula, and symmetry composite.

source.place: Tag 0F14, label lemma-kunneth-one-proper, proof (1), last sentence; Tag 0F0E, label lemma-pull-out-constant; symmetry only reorders the displayed tensor factors

proof.text: To identify the specified map, specialize the current [def-kun-kunneth-map] to $S=\Spec(k)$ and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$. Put $C=Rf_*E\kunotimes{\mathbf Z}Rg_*K$, with $T$ as in step 4. Its map $C\to Rc_*T$ is $Rc_*(\alpha_{E,K})\circ\eta_{c,C}$, where $\alpha_{E,K}$ first applies the inverse monoidality comparison $(\mu^c)^{-1}$, then the canonical composition maps $\gamma_{f,p}\otimes\gamma_{g,q}$, and finally the pulled-back counits $p^{-1}(\varepsilon_{f,E})\otimes q^{-1}(\varepsilon_{g,K})$. Thus it is exactly the adjoint-of-counits map used in clause (a) of [lem-kun-kunneth-map-agrees]. The current definition supplies these composition maps on unbounded constant-coefficient module categories, with their module actions and composite-adjunction units; restricting to the given bounded-below inputs does not change the maps. Under the exact tensor-compatible point equivalence of step 2, the Leray identifications for $f,g,c$ identify $C$ with $A\kunotimes{\mathbf Z}\RGamma(Y_{\Et},K)$ and $Rc_*T$ with $\RGamma(W_{\Et},T)$. Consequently its image is the displayed global-sections morphism $\kappa_{E,K}:A\kunotimes{\mathbf Z}\RGamma(Y_{\Et},K)\to\RGamma(W_{\Et},T)$. Clause (a) of [lem-kun-kunneth-map-agrees] gives $\theta\circ\kappa_{E,K}=\mathrm{id}$ for this very map and the composite of steps 3--6. Clause (a) explicitly requires $Y$ to be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, as assumed here. Its $\ell,e,t,r$ are respectively the canonical comparison of step 5, the exchange map of step 3, the projection-formula map of step 4, and the constant-complex projection map of step 6; its two symmetries are exactly those of step 6. We use its compatibility equation, having independently checked that every factor of $\theta$ is an isomorphism. Multiplying the equation on the left by $\theta^{-1}$ gives $\kappa_{E,K}=\theta^{-1}$, so the specified Kunneth map is an isomorphism.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $k$ be a separably closed
field. Let $X$ be a
proper scheme over $k$
and let $Y$ be a
quasi-compact and
quasi-separated scheme over $k$. If $E\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ has
torsion cohomology and
$K\in\Dplus(Y_{\Et})$, then the Kunneth map of
[def-kun-kunneth-map] for the square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X\times_kY&\xrightarrow{\;\operatorname{pr}_2\;}&Y\\
\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle \operatorname{pr}_1}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle a_Y}\\
X&\xrightarrow{\;a_X\;}&\Spec(k)
\end{array}
$$

$$
\kappa_{E,K}:
\RGamma(X_{\Et},E)\kunotimes{\mathbf Z}\RGamma(Y_{\Et},K)
\longrightarrow
\RGamma\bigl((X\times_kY)_{\Et},
\pr_1^{-1}E\kunotimes{\mathbf Z}\pr_2^{-1}K\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism.

proof.text:
By [lem-kun-proper-stability] the projection
$\operatorname{pr}_2:X\times_kY\to Y$ is proper (base change of the
proper morphism $X\to\Spec(k)$). The object
$\pr_1^{-1}E$ has torsion cohomology and lies in
$\Dplus((X\times_kY)_{\Et})$, so by [lem-kun-0f0f] the
projection formula gives

$$
R\operatorname{pr}_{2,*}
\bigl(\pr_1^{-1}E\kunotimes{\mathbf Z}\pr_2^{-1}K\bigr)
\cong
R\operatorname{pr}_{2,*}\pr_1^{-1}E\kunotimes{\mathbf Z}K .
$$

By proper base change in the form of
[thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below], applied to the cartesian square of
the statement, we have

$$
R\operatorname{pr}_{2,*}\pr_1^{-1}E\cong
\underline{\RGamma(X_{\Et},E)}
$$

(the pullback of a constant object is constant by
[lem-kun-pullback-constant], and the derived global sections of
[def-kun-rgamma-unbounded] compute the sections of
$Ra_{X,*}E$); here $\RGamma(X_{\Et},E)\in\Dplus(\mathbf Z)$ is
bounded below because $E$ is. By [lem-kun-leray-bdd],

$$
\RGamma\bigl((X\times_kY)_{\Et},
\pr_1^{-1}E\kunotimes{\mathbf Z}\pr_2^{-1}K\bigr)
\cong
\RGamma\bigl(Y_{\Et},
\underline{\RGamma(X_{\Et},E)}\kunotimes{\mathbf Z}K\bigr) .
$$

Applying [lem-kun-0f0e] (with $E:=K$ and the constant complex
$\underline{\RGamma(X_{\Et},E)}\in\Dplus(\mathbf Z)$) and then the
symmetry [lem-kun-tensor-sym] we obtain an isomorphism $\theta$
from
$\RGamma((X\times_kY)_{\Et},\pr_1^{-1}E\kunotimes{\mathbf Z}\pr_2^{-1}K)$
to
$\RGamma(X_{\Et},E)\kunotimes{\mathbf Z}\RGamma(Y_{\Et},K)$. By
[lem-kun-kunneth-map-agrees](a),
$\theta\circ\kappa_{E,K}=\mathrm{id}$ (with $\kappa_{E,K}$ the
Kunneth map of [def-kun-kunneth-map]), so $\kappa_{E,K}$ is an
isomorphism, as desired.
